chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Basri, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

When you enter the masjid and the Imam is in ruku', and you think that if you walk toward him he will raise his head before you catch him, then say the takbir and perform ruku'. When he raises his head, then perform sajdah in your place. If he stands, then join the row; and if he sits, then sit in your place; then when he stands, join the row.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the masjid, the place where congregational salat is being performed
key_terms.بِالصَّفِّ: the prayer row of the congregation
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: being in the state of ruku'

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he enters congregational salat while the Imam is in ruku' and fears missing it?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who enters the masjid while the Imam is already in ruku' and fears missing that rak'ah by walking to the row first. It instructs the person to begin immediately where he is, then complete the needed movements and join the row at the appropriate point, showing the practical flexibility of congregational salat rulings.
